newsitem.title: USA: Dell Q2 earnings double, topping estimates.
newsitem.headline: Dell Q2 earnings double, topping estimates.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp said Tuesday its second quarter earnings more than doubled, topping official Wall Street estimates and confirming the strong growth trend in the personal computer industry.

Dell reported second quarter earnings of $214 million or $0.59 per share, up sharply from $103 million or $0.28 a year ago. According to First Call, the consensus Wall Street estimate for Dell's earnings was $0.54 per share.
"I think most people were looking for a modest upside and I think most people got what they wanted," said PaineWebber analyst Walter Winnitzki.
"I think this is further confirmation that the PC industry is doing fine and we may see some acceleration in the second half of the year," he said.

Dell shares initially dipped in after-hours trading, slipping below 84, reflecting the fact that some unofficial "whisper" estimates on the quarter were running at $0.60 a share. But the selling was short-lived, with the shares quickly bouncing back near their closing level of 84-11/16.

Dell's earnings had drawn close attention because of some recent earnings warnings from blue chip companies. Jitters were heightened on Monday when Hewlett-Packard Co posted lower than expected third quarter earnings.

However, H-P's shortfall largely related to slow sales of medical equipment and higher cost levels, while personal computer sales growth actually remained strong, a trend confirmed by Dell's robust sales growth.
Dell's sales surged to $2.8 billion from $1.7 billion a year ago, with sales up 74 percent to nearly $2 billion in the Americas region and 42 percent to $620 million in Europe.
Revenues jumped 89 percent in the Asia-Pacific region to top $200 million and Dell's Internet web site alone is now generating more than $2 million in sales per day.
Gross margin also rose, climbing to 22.2 percent in the quarter from 21.6 percent in the first quarter of the year.

Over the past year, the top personal computer companies have expanded their dominance of the market, usually at the expense of middle-level personal computer companies. That shift benefitted Dell during the first half of the year, a factor the company alluded to in its release.
"During the first half of fiscal 1998, demand remained solid and the market grew at a healthy pace," chairman and chief executive Michael Dell said in a statement.
"The top companies have been consolidating their market share gains during this period and Dell has emerged from this environment as a leader in market share growth," he said.

Analysts also cited a more profitable product mix as aiding the company's outlook. Dell's launch of new high-end network server lines helped server revenues rise 299 percent and servers now account for about eight percent of total systems revenues.
